newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold says Mali gold mine promising.
newsitem.headline: Randgold says Mali gold mine promising.

text.p: Randgold Ltd said on Monday it was satisfied with first indications from its recently acquired Syama gold mine in Mali which were in line with or better than expected.
Randgold Resources chief executive Mark Bristow said the first gold at the Malian mine, taken over by Randgold earlier this month, had been poured.

"While it is early days, our hands-on experience to date has confirmed the potential we found during the due diligence that preceded the acquisition and we're aiming to produce 190,000 ounces of gold at Syama in the 1997 calendar year," Bristow said.

He said the management team at the mine had already began implementing a number of improvements and modifications to operations at Syama which was aimed at reaching production levels of 1.8 million tonnes of ore a year.
Bristow said Randgold had already identified 198 exploration targets in West, East and Central Africa and were busy developing these at different priority levels.
The company had budgeted some 67 million rand for exploration over the next year, he added.
